Three samples of the agent in independent and blind mode and two in seeded mode, over all 24 evaluation papers, against the pipeline on Opus 5.5, which has three samples on all 24 (claims within tolerance of the paper's printed value).  *Agent sample 1* is the row used everywhere else in this report (ROADMAP 3.3, 3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.9); *agent sample 2* is a second Claude Code run: in independent and blind mode `claude-code-run2-13papers-indep-blind-2026-11-01.json` for the 13 earlier papers, `claude-code-run2-4papers-indep-blind-2026-11-02.json` for the four of ROADMAP 3.6 and `claude-code-run2-6papers-indep-blind-2026-11-02.json` for the six of ROADMAP 3.7; in seeded mode `claude-code-run2-23papers-seeded-2026-11-02.json` for the 23 earlier papers (ROADMAP 3.7.2); and `claude-code-run2-1paper-all-modes-2026-11-06.json` in all three modes for the R7 paper (ROADMAP 3.9).  *Agent sample 3* is a third run in independent and blind mode, `claude-code-run3-23papers-indep-blind-2026-11-02.json` for the 23 earlier papers (ROADMAP 3.7.3) and `claude-code-run3-1paper-indep-blind-2026-11-06.json` for the R7 paper; seeded mode has none.  The pipeline samples are those of the table above.  The three columns marked (1, 2) compare agent samples 1 and 2 cell by cell; *identical (all samples)* counts the cells whose final count is the same in every agent sample of that mode.  The last column is the smallest and largest of the agent-minus-pipeline differences over every pairing of an agent sample with a pipeline sample, with the number of pairings in brackets (nine in independent and blind mode, six in seeded).
